2609.24057.title: Representation-guided in-context learning for medical image interpretation with multimodal large language models
2609.24057.paper_summary: Medical image interpretation is central to diagnosis and care, yet adapting general-purpose multimodal large language models (MLLMs) often requires resource-intensive domain-specific fine-tuning. Here we introduce representation-guided in-context learning (RG-ICL), a training-free inference framework that retrieves query-aligned demonstrations using frozen encoders, without task-specific parameter updates. Across eight datasets spanning histopathology, radiology and retinal fundoscopy, RG-ICL improved classification (mean gain 20 percentage points) and visual question answering (VQA) (mean gain 13 percentage points) over no-context and conventional ICL, approaching or exceeding training-based comparators. Which cases were retrieved mattered more than how many: 6 query-aligned cases outperformed up to 32 randomly selected ones, whereas fixed or random cases often reduced accuracy below baseline. For VQA, aligning reference cases with both image content and question intent produced further gains. These findings indicate that for medical image interpretation, curating which reference cases an MLLM sees is a practical alternative to retraining it.
2609.24057.paper_summary_zh: 醫學影像解讀對於診斷和護理至關重要，但調整通用多模態大型語言模型（MLLMs）通常需要資源密集型的特定領域微調。在此，我們介紹了基於表示的上下文學習（RG-ICL），這是一種無需訓練的推理框架，通過使用凍結的編碼器檢索與查詢對齊的示例，而無需特定任務的參數更新。在涵蓋組織病理學、放射學和視網膜底照相的八個數據集上，RG-ICL在分類（平均增益20個百分點）和視覺問題回答（VQA）（平均增益13個百分點）方面優於無上下文和傳統ICL，接近或超過基於訓練的比較方法。檢索哪些案例比檢索多少案例更為重要：6個與查詢對齊的案例的表現超過了多達32個隨機選擇的案例，而固定或隨機案例往往會使準確性降至基線以下。對於VQA，將參考案例與圖像內容和問題意圖對齊可產生進一步的增益。這些發現表明，對於醫學影像解讀，策劃MLLM所見的參考案例是一種實用的替代方案，而不是重新訓練它。
